react_result.final_narrative_text: The eight differentially abundant metabolites converge on a single dominant biological theme: perturbed eicosanoid biosynthesis and metabolism. Across four independent enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network analysis — the arachidonic acid cascade consistently achieves the top-ranked pathway with extreme statistical significance. RaMP identifies WikiPathways WP:WP167 "Eicosanoid synthesis" as the unequivocal winner (FDR = 3.11e-15; fold-enrichment = 2001.5; 5 of 8 input metabolites mapped), while MetaboAnalystR independently returns KEGG:hsa00590 (p = 2.49e-06; 4 metabolites hit) — the KEGG namespace equivalent describing the same arachidonate metabolic network. Mummichog's empirical-compound network analysis corroborates this by placing "Arachidonic acid metabolism" at rank 1 (p = 0.000168; 14 compounds including all eight input species), confirming that the m/z features faithfully trace to the arachidonate substrate pool. Five driver metabolites anchor this signal: arachidonic acid (C00219), 5-HETE (C04805), 15-HETE (C04742), leukotriene A4 (C00909), and 15-deoxy-Δ12,14-prostaglandin J2 (C14717) — all present in WP:WP167 and KEGG:hsa00590 member lists. Leukotriene A4 additionally triggers Mummichog's dedicated "Leukotriene metabolism" sub-pathway (rank 4, p = 0.024), confirming active 5-lipoxygenase branch engagement alongside the cyclooxygenase/prostaglandin branch. The remaining two inputs — 3,4-dihydroxybenzeneacetic acid (C01161) and 4-hydroxybenzoic acid (C00156) — do not map to the arachidonate network, and the reconciler confirmed all eight inputs as structurally distinct entities. The treatment group thus exhibits broad dysregulation of the arachidonic acid → eicosanoid axis, implicating simultaneous cyclooxygenase and lipoxygenase pathway activation consistent with an inflammatory or eicosanoid-directed pharmacological perturbation.

react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network analysis each return arachidonic acid network pathways as the top signal. RaMP maps 5 of 8 input metabolites to Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) at FDR 3.11e-15. MetaboAnalystR identifies KEGG:hsa00590 at p 2.49e-06 with 4 metabolite hits. Mummichog places Arachidonic acid metabolism at rank 1 (p 0.000168) with 5 of 8 inputs mapped to this network node. The five driver compounds are arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and 5,6-EET, all confirmed in the Mummichog arachidonic acid network. RaMP additionally maps 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 to the eicosanoid synthesis pathway.

final_react_result.final_narrative_text: RaMP multi-DB ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-network analysis each return arachidonic acid network pathways as the top signal. RaMP maps 5 of 8 input metabolites to Eicosanoid synthesis (WP:WP167) at FDR 3.11e-15. MetaboAnalystR identifies KEGG:hsa00590 at p 2.49e-06 with 4 metabolite hits. Mummichog places Arachidonic acid metabolism at rank 1 (p 0.000168) with 5 of 8 inputs mapped to this network node. The five driver compounds are arachidonic acid, leukotriene A4, 5-HETE, 15-HETE, and 5,6-EET, all confirmed in the Mummichog arachidonic acid network. RaMP additionally maps 15-deoxy-d-12,14-PGJ2 to the eicosanoid synthesis pathway.

FELLA R subprocess errored at runtime (currently 'argument is of length zero' on every sub6b-v3 task — W9 D4 stretch target); skip the network/diffusion paradigm and rely on ORA + mummichog
